verified.title: v2->v3 migration orphans all real v2 data: rows keep profileId 'local', no profile is created for it, and family members are dropped
verified.evidence:
The v2 app never inserted a profile row. At 0d09358, settings/page-client.tsx:85 only `db.profiles.put(updated)` an existing row. Every write used a hard-coded id: workout-store.ts:168 `profileId: log?.profileId ?? 'local'`, programs/new/page-client.tsx:13 `PROFILE_ID = 'local'`, exercises/[id]/page-client.tsx:112 `profileId: 'local'`.

migrateToV3 builds `profiles` only from the (empty) profiles table (migrations.ts:151-152). For an active program, `owner = profiles.find(...) ?? profiles[0]` is undefined, so no activeProgramId is set (L160-166). Logs are rewritten but keep `profileId: 'local'` (L174-176).

After the upgrade, AppBootstrap calls `ensureActive('Profil 1')`. That finds no live profile and creates a fresh uuid profile (profiles.ts:173). Every read is profile-scoped: logs.list/historyFor go through `[profileId+date]` (logs.ts:73-76), and programs.list/getActive filter by profileId. So all migrated history, programs and notes become unreachable through the repository. The data is still on disk, but no screen, and no `exportBackup(activeId)`, can reach it.

The same upgrade also drops `familyMembers` (and `equipmentProfiles`, `syncMetadata`) with `null` (dexie.ts:125-128) instead of turning family members into v3 profiles. The v2 settings page wrote those rows (settings/page-client.tsx:104). PLAN §6 says the migration is additive.

migration.test.ts:39-55 and 83-90 seed a real profile 'p1' and logs owned by 'p1'. That shape never occurs in v2 data, so the AC18 baseline test is false-green.
verified.reproIdea: Copy the migration.test.ts seedV2 setup with `profiles: []`, `programs: [{id:'prog1', profileId:'local', isActive:true, sessions:[], ...}]` and `workoutLogs: [{...legacyLog, profileId:'local'}]`. Open `new TytaxDatabase(name)`, then run `p = await repo.profiles.ensureActive('Profil 1')`. Expect `await repo.logs.list(p.id)` to be `[]` and `await repo.programs.getActive(p.id)` to be undefined, while `await db.workoutLogs.count()` is 1.
verified.proposedFix: In migrateToV3, first collect every profileId used by owned tables (workoutLogs, programs, exerciseNotes, bodyweightEntries, prRecords, arsenal) that has no profile row. Create a v3 Profile for each one; for 'local', mint a uuid and rewrite profileId on all of its rows, because sync needs uuids. Write `meta.activeProfileId` to that profile, and resolve the isActive program against it. Convert familyMembers rows into profiles (re-owning any log with a matching familyMemberId) before the table is dropped. Replace the migration test fixture with the real v2 shape (no profile rows, profileId 'local').

verdict.how:
I created src/__scratch__/repo-0.test.ts and seeded a v2 database with the exact v1/v2 store specs from migration.test.ts, using the real v2 data shape. There was no profile row. programs had prog1 with profileId 'local' and isActive:true. workoutLogs had log1 with profileId 'local'. exerciseNotes had n1 with profileId 'local'. familyMembers had fm1 with profileId 'local'. I then opened `new TytaxDatabase(name)` and ran `repo.profiles.ensureActive('Profil 1')`. Command: `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/repo-0.test.ts --silent=false`. The test passed (1/1). Output:
  verno: 3; tables no longer include familyMembers (or equipmentProfiles/syncMetadata)
  profilesAfter: [{id:'24d7b11c-…', name:'Profil 1', activeProgramId:null}]
  rawLogCount: 1, rawLogOwner: 'local', rawProgramOwner: 'local', rawNoteCount: 1
  repoLogsForActive: 0, repoProgramsForActive: 0, repoActiveProgram: null
  repoLogsForLocal: ['log1']
So the migrated history, program and notes are still on disk but cannot be reached through the active profile. The family member row is deleted with its table. The claim's premise holds at 0d09358. The only Dexie profile write in v2 is `db.profiles.put(updated)` in settings/page-client.tsx:85, guarded by `if (profile)`. Sync was push-only, so nothing ever inserted a profile row. workout-store.ts:168, programs/new:13, programs:14 and exercises/[id]:112 all hard-code 'local'. PLAN.md:17 itself notes "profileId:'local' not a uuid". So migration.test.ts seeds a profile 'p1' plus 'p1'-owned logs, a shape v2 never produced, and its green result is false. One correction to the claim: an unscoped `repo.exportBackup()` (transfer.ts:57-66, rowsOf without profileId) does include the 'local' rows. The data is hidden, not destroyed, except the familyMembers rows, which are dropped. I deleted the scratch file. src/__scratch__/ still holds other sessions' repo-1/repo-2 files, which I did not touch. I rated it S2, not the claimed S1: PLAN §6 says no deploy is live (the Render service returns 404), and real user data comes from tytax-autonomous through the legacy import, not this migration. It is still a broken spec'd feature (AC18 / G2 item 2) and hides all existing v2 data for any past new_tytax user.
verdict.fix:
src/lib/db/migrations.ts migrateToV3 (owned by G2):
(1) Read familyMembers and the owned tables (workoutLogs, programs, prRecords, bodyweightEntries, exerciseNotes, arsenal) through tx.table() before any rewrite. The familyMembers table is still readable inside the upgrade.
(2) For every distinct profileId that has no profile row, including 'local', mint a uuid Profile (name 'Profil 1' for 'local') and rewrite profileId on every owned row. Use one id map, applied in each table's modify().
(3) Turn each familyMembers row into its own Profile. Re-own logs whose familyMemberId matches, and do it before migrateWorkoutLogRow deletes familyMemberId.
(4) Resolve the isActive program against the re-mapped owner, then put meta {key:'activeProfileId', value:<local's new uuid>} so that ensureActive does not create an empty 'Profil 1'.
(5) In src/lib/db/__tests__/migration.test.ts, replace the fixture with the real v2 shape: profiles: [], profileId 'local', one familyMembers row, and a log carrying familyMemberId. Assert that after ensureActive, repo.logs.list(activeId) returns the log, programs.getActive(activeId) returns prog1, and the family member exists as a profile.

verified.title: PR bests come only from stored PR records, which never follow log edits, deletes, seeded/imported or migrated history, so PR detection gives false or missed PRs
verified.evidence:
finishWorkout computes previous bests only from prRecords: `const stored = await ctx.db.prRecords.where('profileId')...; training.detectPRs(draft.exercises, existingBests(stored))` (finish.ts:71-72). Several paths change history without keeping those records in step:
(a) `logs.update` (logs.ts:92-112) recomputes totals only. PR records, each set's `e1rm`/`isPR` and `prCount` stay as they were. If a fat-fingered 1000x5 bench set is corrected to 100x5, the stored weight PR stays 1000 and no future bench PR is ever detected.
(b) `logs.softDelete` (logs.ts:122-128) tombstones that log's PR records but does not re-derive bests from the remaining logs. Example: w1 100x5 is stored as the baseline; w2 90x5 produces no record. Deleting w1 leaves bench with no live record. w3 at 85x5 then becomes the baseline, and w4 at 88x5 is celebrated as a new PR (prCount 1, isPR) even though live w2 has 90.
(c) Seeded, imported and migrated history carry no PR rows. The e2e `seedHistory` writes logs only (e2e-hooks.ts:102-105). The migration keeps `isPR` on sets but writes no PR records (migrations.ts:86, 178-184). In all three cases the first workout afterwards is a silent baseline, whatever the history holds.
This misleads G3: a pr.spec that seeds a 100 kg history via `tytax.seedHistory` and then finishes 105 kg sees no PR celebration.
verified.reproIdea: Scenario (b) in a vitest case: finish w1 bench 100x5, then w2 90x5, then `repo.logs.softDelete(p, 'w1')`, then finish w3 85x5 and w4 88x5. Expect `(await repo.finishWorkout(w4)).log.prCount` to be 1, which is wrong because live w2 had 90. For (a), `repo.logs.update(p, 'w1', {exercises: fixed})` leaves `repo.prs.best(p, 'bench').weight.value === 1000`.
verified.proposedFix: Pick one source of truth. Either compute `existingBests` inside finishWorkout from the profile's live logs (max e1rm and kg over countsAsWork sets per exerciseId, one scan of the profile's logs, all inside the transaction), or rebuild the PR records of the affected exercises inside logs.update, softDelete, restore and importBackup. In both cases, logs.update must also re-annotate set e1rm/isPR and prCount. Make seedHistory and the migration derive PR records, or rely on the log-derived bests.

verdict.how:
I wrote a scratch test, src/__scratch__/repo-1.test.ts, using the freshRepo, draft and exercise helpers from src/lib/db/__tests__/helpers.ts plus createE2EHooks. I ran it with `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/repo-1.test.ts --silent=false --reporter=verbose`, got 3 passed, and then deleted the file with rm. src/__scratch__/repo-2.test.ts still exists; it belongs to another reviewer and I did not touch it.

The expectations assert the buggy behaviour, so a pass means the bug reproduced. Relevant output:

(b) softDelete. w1 is bench 100x5 and w2 is 90x5.
- After w2: `w2 prs 0 prCount 0`.
- After `logs.softDelete(p,'w1')`: `best after delete w1 {}`.
- w3 (85x5): `w3 prs [["e1rm",95.63,true],["weight",85,true]] prCount 0`, so w3 became a silent baseline.
- w4 (88x5): `w4 prs [["e1rm",99,95.63,false],["weight",88,85,false]] prCount 2 isPR true`.
- `live logs [["w4",88],["w3",85],["w2",90]]`.

Live w2 has 90 kg and an e1RM of 101.25, so both PRs on w4 (88 kg, e1RM 99) are false. This is worse than the claim: prCount is 2, not 1.

(a) logs.update. w1 is bench 1000x5, then corrected to 100 with `logs.update`.
- `updated set {...,"kg":100,"reps":5,"done":true,"e1rm":1125} volume 500`: the set still carries the old e1RM, 1125, where 100x5 gives 112.5.
- `best weight after fix 1000 e1rm 1125`: the PR records stay at the typo values.
- Next workout at 110x5: `w2 (110x5) prs [] prCount 0`. This is a missed PR, and every future bench PR will be missed the same way.

(c) seedHistory. `hooks.seedHistory` seeds bench 100x5, then a 105x5 workout is finished.
- `pr records after seed 0`.
- `105 after seeded 100: prs [["e1rm",118.13,true],["weight",105,true]] prCount 0`. No PR is celebrated, so a G3 pr.spec that seeds a 100 kg history and expects a PR at 105 fails.

The migration part was checked by reading the code, not by running it. migrations.ts keeps set.isPR (line 86) and only patches existing prRecords rows (lines 178-184); it creates none from logs. PLAN.md:15 says the old v2 app never wrote PR records, so every upgraded user starts each exercise from a silent baseline. After that, a lift below their historical max can be celebrated as a PR.

Root cause: finish.ts:71-72 builds existingBests only from the prRecords table. logs.ts update (lines 92-112) recomputes only the totals. softDelete (lines 114-129) tombstones that log's PR records without re-deriving bests from the logs that remain.
verdict.fix:
1. src/lib/db/repo/finish.ts:71-72: stop building the bests from prRecords. Build them from the profile's live logs inside the same transaction. Read `ctx.db.workoutLogs.where('profileId').equals(profileId)`, skip logs with deletedAt, and for each exerciseId take the max `Math.round(training.e1rm(kg,reps)*100)/100` and the max kg over countsAsWork sets with value > 0. Pass that to detectPRs. Existing PR rows then become an audit trail and are no longer the comparison base. This one change fixes (b), fixes (c) for seedHistory, importBackup and migration, and fixes the missed-PR half of (a).
2. src/lib/db/repo/logs.ts update: when `clean.exercises` is set, re-annotate the sets the way annotate() in finish.ts does. That means deleting the stale e1rm and isPR and recomputing e1rm on counting sets. Move annotate into logs.ts and export it.
3. `prs.best`/`prs.list` still read the stale rows. So in logs.update, softDelete and restore, rebuild the PR records of the affected exerciseIds from live logs. Otherwise prs.best would show 1000 after the 100 correction.
4. Add unit tests for scenarios (a), (b) and (c) to src/lib/db/__tests__/finish-workout.test.ts.

Owner: G2 (src/lib/db/**).

verified.title: outbox.peek is not insertion-ordered: same-millisecond ops sort by random uuid, so pr_records can be pushed before the workout_logs row they reference
verified.evidence:
`peek: (limit) => ctx.db.syncQueue.orderBy('createdAt').limit(...)` (transfer.ts:144). Each op gets `createdAt: opts.now().toISOString()` (millisecond precision) and `id: opts.newId()`, a random uuid v4 (context.ts:68-77). The index is `syncQueue: 'id, table, createdAt, recordId'` (dexie.ts:123). IndexedDB orders equal index keys by primary key, so ops that share a millisecond come back in random uuid order.

finishWorkout queues the workout_logs upsert and then the PR upserts a few IDB round-trips apart (finish.ts:98, 118), usually within the same millisecond. With three tied ops, the log comes first only about 1/3 of the time.

The server schema has `workout_log_id uuid references public.workout_logs(id)` (supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:151). A PR pushed first therefore fails its FK, and the ops land in fail/retry with backoff. That contradicts the SyncOutbox contract ("Oldest first") that G5's push relies on.

The tests hide it: the fixed test clock plus sequentialIds give a stable order, and finish-workout.test.ts:211 `.sort()`s the table names before asserting.
verified.reproIdea: Use `createRepository({ db, sync: fakeSync(), now: () => new Date(FIXED) })` with the default `newUuid`. Finish a workout 30 times on fresh DBs and record the index of 'workout_logs' in `(await repo.outbox.peek(10)).map(o => o.table)`. It is not always 0; roughly 2/3 of runs put a pr_records op first.
verified.proposedFix: Give outbox rows a monotonic order key. Options: a per-context counter combined with the stamp, e.g. `seq = ${createdAt}#${String(++counter).padStart(6,'0')}`, in a new indexed field that `peek` orders by; or time-ordered ids (uuidv7/ULID) with `peek` using `orderBy(':id')`. Add a test with random ids that asserts the log comes before its PRs and a program comes before a profile that references it.

verdict.how:
Reproduced the ordering defect. The consequence as claimed (FK failures on about 2/3 of finishes) does not happen with G5's current push; a narrower one does.

Scratch test src/__scratch__/repo-2.test.ts, run with `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/repo-2.test.ts --silent=false --reporter=verbose`, then deleted along with the empty `src/__scratch__` directory. No tracked file was touched. Setup: `createRepository({ db, sync: fakeSync(), now })` with the default `newUuid`, then one profile, then `finishWorkout` of one bench set. That queues 1 workout_logs op and 2 pr_records baseline ops.

Output:
```
sample [["pr_records","2026-03-02T11:00:00.000Z","7930f199"],["workout_logs","2026-03-02T11:00:00.000Z","7ceaee67"],["pr_records","2026-03-02T11:00:00.000Z","ddb7f5f4"]]
FIXED CLOCK idx of workout_logs per run: 1,2,0,2,2,0,1,2,0,2,0,2,0,2,2,1,1,2,0,1,0,1,0,1,2,1,2,0,0,2 | not first: 20 / 30
REAL CLOCK runs where all 3 ops share one ms: 59 / 100 | workout_logs not first: 42 / 100
  (second run: 68/100 share one ms, 49/100 not first)
boundary tail ["pr_records"] total 202
BOUNDARY runs where peek(200) holds a pr_records op but not its workout_logs op: 17 / 20
```

What this shows:
- Ops that share a createdAt come back sorted by uuid, not in the order they were inserted. The sample rows show the ids in ascending order.
- The random ids make this happen with the real clock too: about half of real-clock finishes put a PR ahead of its log. So `transfer.ts:144` breaks the insertion order that `SyncOutbox.peek` "Oldest first" (src/contracts/sync.ts:82) implies.

Why the claimed impact is overstated:
- G5's push (g5/src/lib/sync/push.ts, STEPS/PUSH_ORDER in columns.ts:142) regroups each peeked batch in parent-first table order: profiles, then programs, then workout_logs, then pr_records.
- So when the log and its PRs are in the same batch, the order they were peeked in does not matter. There is no FK failure on about 2/3 of finishes.

The real impact is at the edge of the peek window:
- `collectOps` keeps `live.slice(0, 200)`.
- With 199 or more older ops queued, the window gets a PR op without its log about 2/3 of the time (17/20 in the test above).
- G5 migration 002 keeps a composite FK: `pr_records(workout_log_id, profile_id) -> workout_logs`.
- g5/src/lib/sync/errors.ts lists 23503 (FK violation) in PERMANENT_CODES, so the PR op is dead-lettered and not retried with backoff.
- That PR row then never reaches the server unless it is edited again.
- This needs a backlog of 200 or more ops (weeks offline), so it is rare. When it happens the row is lost from the server silently. This is S3, not S2.
verdict.fix:
In src/lib/db/repo/context.ts, make outbox rows sort in the order they were inserted.

- Option 1, no Dexie schema bump:
  - Keep a module-level counter.
  - Build each outbox row id as `${createdAt}#${String(++seq).padStart(9,'0')}#${opts.newId()}` in `scope.queue()`.
  - IndexedDB breaks equal-createdAt ties by primary key, so `peek`'s `orderBy('createdAt')` in transfer.ts:144 then returns ops in insertion order.
- Option 2: add an indexed `seq` field in a Dexie version(4) and have `peek` use `orderBy('seq')`.

Add a test to src/lib/db/__tests__/finish-workout.test.ts:
- Build the repo with the default newUuid (not sequentialIds) and a fixed clock.
- Loop about 20 times.
- Assert that `peek(1)` after `finishWorkout` returns the workout_logs op.
- Assert that the full `peek` puts workout_logs before every pr_records op, without the `.sort()` used at line 211.

verified.title: NumberField uses type="number", so a decimal comma ("62,5") is silently saved as 0 kg while the field still shows 62,5
verified.evidence: The input is `<input type="number" inputMode={inputMode} …>` (line 74), and `parse` does `Number(trimmed.replace(',', '.'))` (line 28). That replace never runs, because HTML value sanitization for type=number returns `value === ''` for "62,5". I checked this with jsdom (spec-conformant): '62,5' -> '', '62.' -> ''. WebKit/iOS Safari always behaves this way; iOS shows a ',' key on the decimal pad for the hr region. Chromium and Firefox localize the separator from the element language, and the page is `<html lang="en">` (src/app/layout.tsx:32), so ',' is not accepted as a decimal separator there either. The path: `handleChange('')` -> `parse('')` returns undefined -> `onValueChange(undefined)` (lines 64-66) -> set-row.tsx:134 `onChange({ kg: v ?? 0 })` stores kg 0. React does not overwrite a badInput number field whose value is '', so the user keeps seeing "62,5" while the draft holds 0. Ticking done then writes a 0-kg set to history, PRs and volume. A second divergence: when the stored value already equals the clamp bound, out-of-range typing ("-5" on a 0-kg set, "7" on RIR 5) clamps to the same value, the resync check `if (shown !== value)` (line 53) never fires, and the field shows a value the store does not hold. The slice e2e only types '62.5' (e2e/slice.spec.ts:15), so this path is untested.
verified.reproIdea: Vitest: render the SessionExerciseCard from workout-ui.test.tsx, `fireEvent.change(kgInput, {target:{value:'6'}})`, then '62,', then '62,5'. `useWorkoutStore.getState().draft.exercises[0].sets[0].kg` is 0, not 62.5. Playwright on WebKit: `fill('62,5')` on set-kg, click set-done, finish; `listLogs()[0].exercises[0].sets[0].kg === 0`.
verified.proposedFix: Render `type="text" inputMode="decimal"` with `pattern="[0-9]*[.,]?[0-9]*"` and keep `parse`, so a comma works. Treat an unparsable string, or `e.currentTarget.validity.badInput`, as 'keep the last value', never as a clear. On blur or after a clamp, always resync the text to `format(value)` so the field cannot show a value the store does not hold. Add unit and e2e cases for '62,5'.

verdict.how:
I reproduced this in vitest/jsdom with a temporary file, src/__scratch__/ui-store-0.test.ts, which I have since deleted. The test rendered SessionExerciseCard on the real workout store and a fake-indexeddb repository, then ran `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/ui-store-0.test.ts --disableConsoleIntercept --reporter=verbose`. All 3 cases passed and printed:
```
typed="6"    input.value="6"  store.kg=6
typed="62"   input.value="62" store.kg=62
typed="62,"  input.value=""   store.kg=0
typed="62,5" input.value=""   store.kg=0
log set: kg=0 reps=8 done=true totalVolumeKg=0
one-shot: input.value="" store.kg=0
rir: input.value=7 store.rir=5; kg: input.value=-5 store.kg=0
```
**What this shows:**
- **Typing key by key:** at "62," the type=number value is sanitised to "". handleChange('') then calls parse('') → undefined, and set-row.tsx:47 stores `kg: v ?? 0`. At "62,5" the value is still "", so React's value tracker sees no change and onChange never fires. After set-done, repo.finishWorkout writes a done set with kg 0 and totalVolumeKg 0 to the log.
- **Pasting or filling "62,5" in one go:** onChange never fires, so the store keeps its previous kg. That is 0 here. It would be the copied last-set kg after add-set.
- **Field still shows "62,5":** jsdom can't show the visible text apart from .value, so I confirmed this from React's code instead. In node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:1662-1664, a number input's value is written only if `element.value != value`. Here both are "", so the browser's bad-input text stays on screen.
- **Real browsers:** Blink and WebKit behave the same when lang="en" (layout.tsx:32). The en locale treats ',' as a group separator, so the browser does not convert the text and sanitises the value to "". I argued this from the engines' number-localisation logic. I did not run it, because running Playwright is not allowed here.
- **Why it matters:** Croatian is the default language (PLAN D3). An iOS decimal pad for the hr region shows only ','.
- **Second claim, also reproduced:** with RIR at 5, typing "7" leaves the store at 5 and the field showing 7. With kg at 0, typing "-5" leaves the store at 0 and the field showing -5. The resync check at number-field.tsx:53 never fires because the clamped value equals the old one.

**Severity:** S2, not S1. The app is not deployed, and whole-number weights and '.' entry work. It is still silent wrong data on the main set-logging path for the default locale, and it has to be fixed before G2/G3 build on it. The clamp divergence alone would be S3.

**Not covered:** debrief-form.tsx:71 (RPE) also uses type="number", but it takes whole numbers only, so this bug does not apply there.
verdict.fix:
In src/components/workout/number-field.tsx:
1. **Input type:** render `type="text"` and keep `inputMode={inputMode}`. Add `pattern` / `autoComplete="off"`. Drop step/min/max as DOM attributes and keep them for the clamp only. This makes the browser pass "62,5" through, and parse() already turns ',' into '.'.
2. **Unparsable text:** in handleChange, keep `if (n === null) return;`. That keeps the last good value and never clears it.
3. **Clamp resync:** after clamping, if `clamped !== n`, call `setText(format(clamped, zeroIsEmpty))`. This covers a clamp to the same bound, where the `shown !== value` check never fires. Also add an onBlur that resyncs the text to `format(value, zeroIsEmpty)` whenever `parse(text)` does not equal the value.
4. **Tests:** update the NumberField tests in src/components/workout/__tests__/workout-ui.test.tsx. They use `toHaveValue(number)`, which becomes a string once the input is type=text. Add unit cases for "62,5" → 62.5, for a partial "62," that keeps 62, and for "7" on RIR 5 that shows 5.
5. **E2E:** add a row with '62,5' to ENTERED_SETS in e2e/slice.spec.ts, and assert the log holds 62.5.

verified.title: The workout draft is not scoped to the active profile: after a profile switch the workout is saved to the old profile, and after that profile is deleted it can never be saved
verified.evidence: The draft carries `profileId`, but no consumer compares it with the active profile. /workout shows `draft ? <current-draft …>` (workout/page-client.tsx:104). AddToWorkoutButton adds to any existing draft (add-to-workout-button.tsx:27-32). Debrief calls `finishWorkout(current, debrief)`, and finish.ts:64-65 uses `draft.profileId` and `getLiveProfile(ctx, profileId)`. Settings switch and delete (family-section.tsx:44-54, profiles.ts remove) never touch the persisted draft. Scenario 1: profile A starts a workout, the user switches to B in settings, B continues and finishes. The log is written to A, and `router.replace('/history')` lists B's logs, so the workout seems to vanish. Scenario 2: A is deleted before finishing. `getLiveProfile` throws NOT_FOUND on every save, the debrief shows only `t('error')`, and the only way out is Discard on /workout, which loses the workout.
verified.reproIdea: Vitest with fake-indexeddb: create profiles A and B, `startQuick(A)`, `setActive(B)`, render DebriefPage and save. `logs.list(B)` is empty and `logs.list(A)` has 1. Then `profiles.remove(A)` before saving: `finishWorkout` rejects with RepoError NOT_FOUND.
verified.proposedFix: Make the store contract profile-aware. Have /workout, dashboard, AddToWorkoutButton and debrief treat `draft.profileId !== activeProfileId` as 'draft belongs to <name>' and offer switch-back or discard, not continue. Block profile switch or delete (or prompt) while a draft for that profile exists, or discard it inside `profiles.remove`. Show a specific error on NOT_FOUND.

verdict.how:
I created src/__scratch__/ui-store-1.test.ts. It used fake-indexeddb/auto, the real getRepository() singleton, the real persisted useWorkoutStore, and rendered the real WorkoutPage and DebriefPage. Only next/navigation and @/lib/catalog were mocked. I ran `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/ui-store-1.test.ts --reporter=verbose --silent=false` and both tests passed (2/2). Then I deleted the file with rm, and src/__scratch__ no longer exists.

verified.title: test.fail()/it.fails are not banned, and test.fail() also switches off the >=3-expects check
verified.evidence: SKIPPERS = "/^(skip|only|fixme|todo|skipIf|runIf)$/" does not include fail or fails. In e2e/fixtures/test.ts:45 the counter only runs when `testInfo.status === 'passed' && testInfo.expectedStatus === 'passed'`, and Playwright's test.fail() sets expectedStatus='failed' (testInfo.js:181). As a result, `test('x', async ({page}) => { test.fail(); await expect(page).toHaveURL('/x'); })` and `test.fail('c', ...)` run as expected failures: the list reporter marks them passed and the exit code is 0. Vitest's `it.fails(...)` / `test.fails(...)` also reports a broken body as passing. I checked this with `npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename e2e/probe.spec.ts` and `--stdin-filename src/lib/probe.test.ts`: both lint with 0 errors for these forms (the only error was on test.skip). A goal that cannot fix a feature overnight can therefore write test.fail() and still get a green gate.
verified.reproIdea: `printf "import { test, expect } from './fixtures';\ntest('b', async ({ page }) => { test.fail(); await expect(page).toHaveURL('/nope'); });\n" | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename e2e/x.spec.ts` gives rc=0. Running that spec with Playwright reports 1 passed.

In e2e/fixtures/test.ts, make the _minExpects teardown throw when `testInfo.expectedStatus !== 'passed'`, so an expected-failure annotation can never produce a green result.

Running `it.fails` and `test.fails` through `--stdin-filename src/lib/probe.test.ts` returned rc=0 with no output.

2) Vitest (scratch file, since deleted). src/__scratch__/harness-0.test.ts contained a broken `add` (`a+b-1`) plus `it.fails('…', () => expect(add(1,2)).toBe(3))` and `test.fails(…)`. `npx eslint` on it returned eslint_rc=0. `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/harness-0.test.ts` printed "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 2 expected fail (2)" with vitest_rc=0. So a broken feature gives a green lint and a green unit suite. I then ran `rm`, and `ls` confirmed harness-0.test.ts is gone.

3) Playwright. I did not run it, because the brief forbids it. The behaviour is proven from the installed source (v1.58.2):
- node_modules/playwright/lib/worker/testInfo.js:180-181: `fail` sets `expectedStatus="failed"`.
- teleReceiver.js computeTestCaseOutcome:497: `result.status === test.expectedStatus` counts as `expected`, so `ok()` is true and the exit code is 0.

A test.fail() test whose assertions fail is therefore reported as expected and CI stays green. CI runs this suite (`npx playwright test --project=chromium`, `npm run lint`).

Correction to the claim: the `expectedStatus==='passed'` clause at e2e/fixtures/test.ts:45 is not what opens the hole. With test.fail() and a failing body, `testInfo.status` is already 'failed', so the >=3-expects check would be skipped anyway. With a passing body, Playwright already reports "unexpected". The loophole is the fail annotation itself.

The proposed teardown fix also would not work as written. Throwing in teardown leaves status='failed', which still equals expectedStatus='failed', so the result is still "expected". The runner copies expectedStatus from the worker payload (workerMain.js:504, dispatcher.js:268), so the fixture has to reset it.

The existing `repo.outbox.fail()` is not matched, because its object is not a runner name.
2) eslint.config.mjs:21-22: change `/^(skip|fixme)$/` to `/^(skip|fixme|fail)$/` so that testInfo.fail() and test.info().fail() are also banned. Update SKIP_MESSAGE to mention .fail/.fails.

This path runs in the shipped app. src/data/bodyweight/presets.ts ('bw-fundamentals') has slots with modality 'bodyweight' (for example bw_push_standard-push-up). verified.title: ACWR has no cold-start handling, so a new user's first session marks every trained muscle 'fried' (legacy had a floor)
verified.evidence: chronicLoad is `sum/4` over 28 days, which includes the acute week, and ratio is `acuteLoad / chronicLoad` (lines 57-59). With under 3 weeks of history the ratio is inflated: one log gives ratio 4 and 'fried'. The test pins this: acwr.test.ts:64 '// … ratio 4 → fried'. Two steady weeks give ratio 2 and 'fried' (acwr.test.ts 'only done working sets' case). Probe: the first session of every built-in preset (tytax-elite-v3 Upper A, bw-fundamentals, all three KB presets) gives acwr statuses ['fried'] and ratio 4. The legacy app used a protocol-baseline chronic floor and looser new-user thresholds (legacy index.html:6305-6352) to prevent this. G4's dashboard and any deload prompt tied to 'fried' (as legacy did at index.html:6166) will warn every new user.

verified.proposedFix: If the earliest live log is fewer than 21–28 days before `now`, return status 'fresh' (or add an optional `insufficientHistory: true` / ratio null) instead of classifying. verdict.how:
I wrote a scratch test at src/__scratch__/contracts-engine-8.test.ts and ran `npx vitest run src/__scratch__/contracts-engine-8.test.ts --reporter=verbose --silent=false`. It passed 2 of 2, and I deleted the file afterwards. The only files I touched were my own scratch file; the other files in src/__scratch__ belong to other refuters. For each built-in preset, the probe took the first non-rest session, logged it one day before now with every set done, and looked exercises up in the real catalog. The output:
PRESET tytax-original-6day / Upper A: muscles=9 statuses=["fried"] ratios=[4]
PRESET tytax-elite-v3 / Upper A: muscles=10 statuses=["fried"] ratios=[4]
PRESET bw-fundamentals / Full Body A: muscles=13 statuses=["fried"] ratios=[4]
PRESET kb-simple-sinister / kb-hypertrophy / kb-conditioning: statuses=["fried"] ratios=[4]
ONE LOG, ONE SET: {"muscle":"Biceps","acuteLoad":1,"chronicLoad":0.25,"ratio":4,"status":"fried","trend":"rising"}

For comparison, the older session-level ACWR in the same diff (src/lib/analytics/acwr.ts:67) already treats a single training day as ratio 1 ("optimal"): `computeACWR single day: [[1,"optimal"]]`.
Cause: acwr.ts:58 always divides the chronic sum by 4. The acute week is part of the 28-day window, so with less than 21 days of history the ratio can only be 4 (one week of history) or 2 (two weeks). Any steady new user is shown as 'fried' on every trained muscle for their first 14 days. The tests pin this: acwr.test.ts:57 ("ratio 4/2 = 2 → fried") and :64 ("ratio 4 → fried").
Why S3 and not S2: neither the spec (GOALS G1.5, PLAN AC7) nor the contract (training.ts:160) asks for cold-start handling, and nothing in Wave 0 uses training.acwr yet (the analytics page uses computeACWR). The reviewer says the deload prompt is tied to this. That was true in legacy, where index.html:6166 read the ACWR-based status that had a cold-start floor. In v2 the deload offer is tied to recoveryStatus (GOALS G3.1, "when recovery is fried"), a separate 48-hour load rule, not to ACWR. The harm is a false 'fried' warning once G4 wires ACWR into analytics or the dashboard.
verdict.fix:
This keeps the ACWRResult shape unchanged. In src/lib/training/acwr.ts, while looping over live logs, also track the earliest live log time t0 at or before now. Take this from all logs, not only those inside the 28-day window, so a user returning from a break keeps the 4-week denominator. Set `weeks = Math.min(4, Math.max(1, Math.ceil((nowMs - t0) / (7 * DAY_MS))))` and change line 58 to `chronicLoad = clean(sum / weeks)`. The result: one log gives ratio 1 ('recovering'), two steady weeks give ratio 1, and users with 4 or more weeks of history are unaffected. Update the doc comments in acwr.ts:37 and in contracts/domain.ts, where ACWRResult.chronicLoad reads "Mean weekly load over the last 28 days", to say "over the weeks of history covered (max 4)". Re-derive the tests in src/lib/training/__tests__/acwr.test.ts:
- 'only done working sets' (10-day span, so weeks=2): chronic 8/2=4, ratio 1, 'recovering'.
- 'one row per standardised muscle' (weeks=1): chronic equals acute, ratio 1.
- 'thresholds are strict' (20-day span): add an older log more than 28 days back so the /4 denominator stays and the 1.5 and 0.8 edges are still tested.
- Add a new case: a single log yesterday is not 'fried'.
Do not add the legacy protocol-baseline floor, because it needs the active program and would change the AcwrFn signature.

s3.title: Finishing a draft with zero done sets saves an empty log and advances the program rotation; Finish is the only exit on the active page
s3.evidence: `finish-workout` is always enabled (lines 79-87). DebriefForm has no guard. `finishWorkout` accepts `exercises: []` or all-undone sets and writes a log with `totalSets: 0`, then runs `if (draft.programId) … advanceIn(...)` (finish.ts:121-127). The active page has no discard or cancel control; discard exists only on /workout. So a program session started by mistake and 'finished' out of it is skipped in the rotation, and an empty session shows in history and in the dashboard's weekly count.

s3.title: The store and repo count done sets with 0 reps, but the training engine excludes them; prefilled sets make 0-rep done sets likely
s3.evidence: `countsAsWork(s) = s.done && s.type !== 'warmup'` (workout-selectors.ts:17-19). The same rule is duplicated in repo/logs.ts:19-21 and feeds `computeTotals` -> `log.totalSets`. training/common.ts:14-16 `isDoneWorkingSet` also requires `s.reps > 0`, and that rule feeds PRs, ACWR, recovery and prefill. Prefill creates sets with `reps: 0` and shows last time's reps only as a placeholder (`placeholder={ghostReps}`, `zeroIsEmpty`, set-row.tsx:139-141). A user who taps done over the ghost value therefore records a 0-rep done set. The debrief 'sets' stat and history `totalSets` count it; PR, ACWR and next-session prefill ignore it. G3 and G4 inherit two different definitions of a 'done working set'.
s3.reproIdea: Vitest: a draft with one done set `{kg:60,reps:0,type:'working',done:true}`. `summarizeDraft(d).doneSets === 1` and `computeTotals(d.exercises).totalSets === 1`, but `training.detectPRs(d.exercises, {})` is empty and the ACWR set count is 0.
s3.proposedFix: Pick one rule in contracts/training.ts (recommended: done && working/drop/failure && reps > 0) and have the selectors and repo import the training predicate, not re-implement it. In the UI, either block done while reps is 0 or adopt the ghost reps when done is tapped on an empty reps field.

s3.title: Discarding the in-progress workout takes one tap with no confirmation, and the button sits directly under Continue

s3.title: The sync cursor contract has no tiebreaker id, the server stamps whole transactions with one updated_at, and Dexie keys cursors by table only
s3.evidence: `SyncCursor { table; accountId; lastPulledAt: string | null; lastPushedAt }` (sync.ts:55-61) is timestamp-only. The server trigger sets `new.updated_at = now()` (supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:215), which is the transaction start time, so all rows upserted in one push (for example the N pr_records from one finishWorkout) share one updated_at. A paged keyset pull with `updated_at > lastPulledAt` skips the rest of a group split at a page boundary; with `>=` a full page of equal timestamps loops. AC12 requires a retry cursor. Also, Dexie declares `syncCursors: 'table'` (src/lib/db/dexie.ts:124), although the cursor carries accountId, so signing in with a second account on the same device reuses the first account's cursor and never pulls the second account's older rows.
s3.reproIdea: Insert 3 rows in one transaction into workout_logs on local Supabase, then pull with limit 2 and `gt('updated_at', cursor)` using the last row's updated_at as the cursor. The third row is never returned. For Dexie: put cursors {table:'workout_logs',accountId:'A'} then {…,'B'} and count() returns 1.
s3.proposedFix: Add the optional field `lastPulledId?: string` to SyncCursor and pull ordered by (updated_at, id) with `(updated_at, id) > (cursor, lastId)`, or use clock_timestamp() in the trigger. Key syncCursors by `[table+accountId]`.

s3.title: CI retries mark failing-then-passing e2e tests green (no failOnFlakyTests)
s3.evidence: `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` without `failOnFlakyTests`. In Playwright 1.58 (runner/failureTracker.js:57) a test that fails and then passes on retry is 'flaky', and the run status is 'passed' unless config.failOnFlakyTests is set. Any intermittent defect, such as timing around the reload/persist step the slice spec exists to prove, passes CI on the second attempt. Specs can also add `test.describe.configure({ retries: n })`, which the lint does not ban.
s3.reproIdea: Run a spec that fails on attempt 1 and passes on attempt 2 (e.g. branch on testInfo.retry) with CI=1: Playwright prints '1 flaky' and exits 0.
s3.proposedFix: Set `failOnFlakyTests: !!process.env.CI`, or keep retries in CI only for trace capture while failing on flaky. Ban `describe.configure` with retries in e2e lint.

s3.title: PORT falls back to 3100, the G5 integration port, when unset

s3.title: SHA guard ignores working-tree state, so a stale E2E_SERVER=prod build from the same HEAD passes
s3.evidence: Both sides compare plain `git rev-parse HEAD` (next.config.ts:14 at config load, global-setup.ts:24 at run time). No dirty marker or tree hash is included. With `E2E_SERVER=prod` (playwright.config.ts:19-21, `next start` serving whatever `.next` exists), a build made at HEAD X before uncommitted edits still reports sha X. The guard passes and the run tests the old bytes, a green that says nothing about the current source. In dev mode the same blindness means the SHA pasted as evidence in reports and signals does not identify the bytes that were tested.
s3.reproIdea: Run `NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_HOOKS=1 npm run build`, edit a component without committing, then `E2E_SERVER=prod PORT=3101 npx playwright test`: the guard passes and the edit is not what was tested.
s3.proposedFix: Report a content-aware id on both sides, e.g. HEAD plus a hash of `git diff HEAD` and untracked files (or `git describe --always --dirty`), and fail on mismatch. In prod mode, also refuse to run when the working tree is dirty or when `.next/BUILD_ID` is older than the newest tracked-file mtime.

s3.title: importBackup checks only id and profileId; malformed rows are stored and then break reads for that profile
s3.evidence:
validateBackup accepts any row that is an object with a non-empty string `id` (and a string `profileId` outside profiles) (transfer.ts:29-31, 84-91). Rows are then `bulkPut` verbatim (L109).

A workoutLogs row `{id:'x', profileId:p, date:'2026-03-01'}` imports as `{inserted:1}`. Afterwards `logs.historyFor(p, 'bench')` rejects with a TypeError at logs.ts:151 (`l.exercises.some`), and every history view that reads `log.exercises` crashes for the whole profile.

A row without `date` falls out of the `[profileId+date]` index: `logs.list(p)` hides it (logs.ts:73-76) while `logs.count(p)` still counts it (L155-157).

A profile row without `settings` imports cleanly, after which every `updateSettings` call fails VALIDATION in mergeSettings (profiles.ts:38-41), and UI reads of `profile.settings.units` throw.

This is the only validation on the JSON restore path (G2 AC18: a failed import must leave the DB unchanged; PLAN §7 lists malicious import JSON as an abuse path).
s3.reproIdea: Call `repo.importBackup({format:'tytax-backup', version:3, exportedAt:'x', profiles:[], workoutLogs:[{id:'x', profileId:p.id, date:'2026-03-01'}], programs:[], prRecords:[], bodyweightEntries:[], exerciseNotes:[], arsenal:[], equipment:[]})`. It resolves `{inserted:1, updated:0}`. Then `await repo.logs.historyFor(p.id, 'bench')` rejects with a TypeError, which is not a RepoError.
s3.proposedFix: Validate each table's rows against its domain shape before opening the transaction: required fields, types, calendar-day `date`, ISO timestamps, `exercises` array through validateExercises, and full `settings` through mergeSettings/validateSettings. Throw RepoError('VALIDATION') naming the first bad row.

s3.title: Read methods and exportBackup bypass wrapStorage, so storage failures surface as raw DexieError instead of RepoError('STORAGE')
s3.evidence:
wrapStorage, which maps DexieError to RepoError('STORAGE'), is applied only in ctx.write and ctx.transaction (context.ts:83, 93). Every read calls Dexie directly and is not wrapped: logs.list/get/historyFor/count (logs.ts:81-158), profiles.list/get/getActiveId (profiles.ts:92-160), programs.list/getActive, prs, bodyweight/notes/arsenal/equipment reads, outbox.peek/count, and exportBackup (transfer.ts:37-69).

The frozen contract says "Failures throw `RepoError` with a typed `code`" (repo.ts:15). When IndexedDB cannot open (private mode, blocked storage, a VersionError from an old tab), `useRepoQuery` consumers receive a Dexie OpenFailedError/MissingAPIError, and `isRepoError(e, 'STORAGE')` is false. The same failure on a write is a RepoError, so error UIs keyed on codes (G4) only handle half the cases.
s3.reproIdea: `vi.spyOn(db.workoutLogs, 'where').mockImplementation(() => { throw new Dexie.OpenFailedError('x') })`. Expect `repo.logs.list(pid)` to reject with an error for which `isRepoError(e, 'STORAGE')` is false. The same spy on a write path, e.g. `bodyweight.add` via `db.bodyweightEntries.add`, gives a RepoError STORAGE.
s3.proposedFix: Wrap every public repository method with wrapStorage, for example by wrapping the method objects once in createRepository, so reads, exportBackup and outbox calls also map DexieError to RepoError('STORAGE').

s3.title: Global outerDepth drops the sync notification of an unrelated committed write when a concurrent repo.transaction fails
s3.evidence: `outerDepth`/`pendingNotify` are closure-global (context.ts:36-37), not tied to a transaction. Take a write W (for example `bodyweight.add` with sync enabled) that starts before a `repo.transaction(fn)` call. The transaction increments outerDepth synchronously (L90) and waits for the IndexedDB lock. W then commits and calls `notify()`, which sees `outerDepth > 0`, sets `pendingNotify = true` and returns (L40-42). If fn then throws, `shouldNotify = pendingNotify && ok` is false and pendingNotify is cleared (L99-101). W's committed outbox rows are never announced through `notifyChanged()`, breaking the contract rule that the repository notifies after a committed mutation that queued ops (sync.ts:97).
s3.reproIdea: With `fakeSync()`: `const w = repo.bodyweight.add(p, {...}); const t = repo.transaction(async () => { throw new Error('x') }).catch(() => {}); await Promise.all([w, t]);`. Expect `sync.notifyChanged` not to have been called for W's committed op.
s3.proposedFix: Decide whether a write joined an outer transaction from the Dexie zone (`Dexie.currentTransaction` at the start of ctx.write), not from a global counter. Notify immediately after commit for top-level writes; accumulate a pending flag per outer transaction only for joined writes.
